question.text: The State of Lu's official chronicle, the Annals, provided the name for a "period" where the Eastern Zhou began named after two of these time periods-spring and autumn.
question.clue: To display the Emerald Buddha in Wat Phra Kaew, Rama I and Rama III constructed three sets of decorations based on these time periods, including a "rainy" example characterized by monsoons.

swap.leadin: During this rebellion, a Muslim group called the Hansu Braves set fire to Hanlin Academy during the Siege of the Foreign Legations.
swap.text: Name this rebellion which occurred during the Qing [Ching] dynasty and was defeated by the Eight-Nation Alliance.
swap.answerHtml: Boxer Rebellion [or Boxer Uprising; or other synonyms for “rebellion;” or Yihetuan Movement]
swap.clue: The young girls who made up the Red Lanterns of the group that names this event supposedly could stop bullets with their fans.

question.text: The construction of over six thousand backyard steel furnaces was a part of this economic policy by which Mao planned for China to modernize in a short period of time.
question.answerHtml: Great Leap Forward [also accept Second Five-Year Plan or Dayuejin]
question.clue: This period grew out of a conference in the resort city of Qingdao and the Anti-Rightist Campaign.

swap.text: Rustichello da Pisa wrote a travelogue about this man's journey to China, where he lived in the court of Kublai Khan.
swap.clue: Two Dominican monks and gifts from Pope Gregory X were carried east by Maffeo and Niccolo, who were this man's uncle and father, respectively.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the various conquests of the Khans not named Genghis.
question.text: This Khan established the Yuan Dynasty after conquering the Song Dynasty of China.
question.clue: After winning a succession war against his brother Ariq Boke, he conquered southern China with his pyro-curious general Bayan Hundred Eyes.

swap.text: The treaty ending the First Opium War was signed in this city. It was later the capital of the Kuomintang regime before and after the Second Sino-Japanese War.
swap.clue: A contest to kill one hundred people with a sword took place in this city, which was once the site of the Porcelain Tower.

question.leadin: Participants in this rebellion were at first primarily of the Hakka ethnicity.
question.text: Name this massive and bloody 19th-century rebellion against the Qing Dynasty led by Hong Xiuquan, who declared himself ruler of a Heavenly Kingdom.
question.clue: This rebellion began among the Hakka people, and it at first advocated the segregation of men and women and the abolishment of private property.

swap.leadin: This explorer of Muslim descent brought back ivory, ostriches, zebras, and a giraffe, among other things.
swap.text: Name this Chinese court eunuch and admiral, who traveled as far as Africa while leading seven voyages across the Indian Ocean.
swap.clue: A controversial 2002 work by Gavin Menzies claimed that this man discovered the Americas, Australia, and the Northeast Passage.

question.leadin: It prohibited any large country from claiming an exception from taxes on harbor and railroad usage.
question.text: Name this policy formulated by Secretary of State John Hay, which also stated that China's independence should be respected and all nations should have equal access to trade in China.
question.clue: This doctrine, formulated by John Hay, demanded that all countries be given equal access to commerce in China and that only China itself could collect taxes on merchants.

swap.leadin: These people, under Yelu Dashi, moved to Central Asia and formed an eponymous "Kara Khanate."
swap.text: Name these people, originally from Manchuria, who began that khanate after defeating the Karakhanids and capturing Balasagun. These people's name is the origin of the historic name "Cathay" for China.
swap.clue: They divided their holdings into the Northern and Southern Chancellories and their emperors included men such as Shengzong and Jingzong, while their first ruler took the name Taizu and was known as Abaoji.

question.leadin: During this event, there was a skirmish to secure the Luding Bridge.
question.text: Name this 1930's event. Its most famous component featured a group fleeing from Jiangxi to Shaanxi to avoid the pursuing Kuomintang forces.
question.clue: The Fifth Encirclement forced this event, which Otto Braun took part in. The participants of this event defeated warlord forces at the Battle of Luding Bridge and reshuffled their leadership at the Zunyi Conference.

swap.leadin: The New Fourth Army incident occurred during a theoretical suspension of this conflict.
swap.text: Name this war that lasted, off and on, from 1927 to 1950. It ended with the Kuomintang forced to set up a new government after being forced out of the mainland.
swap.clue: Leaders of one side in this war were interviewed by Edgar Snow at their base in Yan'an.

question.leadin: A popular Han dynasty text was titled for the biographies of "virtuous" examples of these people.
question.text: Name these people, who were the subject of numerous "chastity arches" built during the Ming dynasty. These people were subjected to the painful practice of foot-binding.

swap.text: After passing the final Metropolitan Exam, candidates were awarded this highest and final degree. The purchasing of this degree toward the end of the Qing (ching) meant the "Imperial Scholars" who held it were no longer guaranteed the highest offices.
swap.clue: Original-language term required. This highest degree of the imperial examination was extremely difficult, but passing it made one a member of China's bureaucratic elite. The emperor himself sometimes proctored this degree's exam.

question.text: Exaggerated accounts of King Zhou's reign come from this history written by Sima Qian ("SUH-mah chee-EN"). It spans from the reign of the Yellow Emperor to Emperor Wu.
question.clue: This text describes the melting of thousands of enemy weapons to create twelve colossal metal statues, a loyalty test in which a man points to a deer and calls it a horse, and the "rectification of weights and measures."

swap.leadin: The "peach-plum prophecy," which cryptically suggested that someone with this family name would overthrow the Sui, was fulfilled by Gaozu's founding of the Tang dynasty.
swap.text: Give this family name. Much later, having this auspicious family name helped a "dashing prince" to assemble a rebel army that overthrew the Ming dynasty and installed him as emperor of the short-lived Shun dynasty.
swap.clue: A powerful governor of the Longxi Commandery from this family used Gokturk support to install the puppet emperor Yang You before toppling him and establishing a ruling dynasty.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a Chinese province.
question.text: The Xiang River runs through this Chinese province whose name means "south of the lake" due to its proximity to Lake Dongting. Mao Zedong established a short-lived namesake soviet here in 1927 after the Autumn Harvest Uprising.

swap.leadin: This building was heavily looted in 1959 after thousands of protestors gathered in front of it during Women's Uprising Day.
swap.text: The white section of what building, the Potrang Karpo, became a seat of government in 1649? The red section, the Potrang Marpo, was added in the 1690s.

question.leadin: This man kept his father Ruizong on as "Supreme Emperor" after Ruizong's abdication.
question.text: Identify this long-ruling emperor of the Tang dynasty whose later years were dominated by the policies of Li Linfu. He also appointed future rebel An Lushan as a general.
question.clue: Late in his reign, he began to favor the chancellor Yang Guozhong, a cousin of his favorite concubine, Yang Guifei, one of the Four Beauties of China.

swap.text: Tsai was a chief drafter of the special state-to-state relations doctrine pursued by this predecessor of Chen. Nicknamed "Mr. Democracy," this first directly elected President of Taiwan partially initiated the Third Taiwan Straits Crisis by making a 1995 visit to his alma mater, Cornell.
swap.clue: In the 1980s, this person nicknamed "Mr. Democracy" asserted that his country's claims to the Spratly Islands were exactly the same as China's. This person's trip to his alma mater Cornell in 1995 precipitated a military standoff between China and the US.
